You are being evaluated on Continual-ARC, a lifelong stream of ARC-style grid puzzles.
Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: an instance you solve costs 1 for each wrong submission and 1 for
each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

A uniform separator row or column divides the grid into two equal-sized panels; omit it and compare cells at identical coordinates. Each panel is binary; let S be the single color shared by both panels. Output has one panel’s dimensions, is filled with color 3, and uses S at each coordinate where EITHER corresponding input cell is not S. Equivalently: output 3 only where BOTH corresponding cells equal S; otherwise output S. Do not reverse these output colors. Examples: demo with S=9 outputs 3 at common-background locations, 9 where either panel has a non-9 speckle. Confirmed test with upper colors {8,1}, lower {1,4}, separator row [0,0], S=1; compare top rows 0–13 to input rows 15–28. Correct output: [[1,1],[1,3],[1,3],[1,1],[1,3],[1,1],[1,1],[3,1],[1,1],[3,1],[1,1],[1,3],[1,3],[1,1]]. Careful: bottom panel starts immediately after separator (row 15 in this 0-indexed 29x2 case); map all 14 rows in order.

Additional confirmed recurrence (task-638c72af, test input 2x19): a zero separator column divides two 2x9 panels. Left panel uses {6,7}, right uses {4,6}, so the shared color is S=6. Compare identical coordinates: output is 3 only where both panel cells equal 6, otherwise 6. Row 0 had no coordinate where both were 6, yielding [6,6,6,6,6,6,6,6,6]; row 1 shared 6 only at column 3, yielding [6,6,6,3,6,6,6,6,6]. Submission was confirmed correct.

Additional confirmed recurrence (29x2): [8,8] separator row at index 14 splits 14x2 panels (top rows 0–13, bottom rows 15–28). Top colors {7,9}, bottom {5,7}, shared S=7. Apply rule rowwise: output 3 iff both aligned cells are 7, else 7. Confirmed correct output: [[7,3],[3,7],[3,7],[7,3],[3,7],[7,3],[7,3],[3,3],[3,7],[3,3],[7,3],[7,3],[3,7],[7,7]].


Additional confirmed recurrence (15x14): uniform separator row at index 7 splits two 7x14 panels; colors top {8,1}, bottom {7,1}, shared S=1. Output remains 7x14 and is 3 only at coordinates where both aligned cells are 1, otherwise 1. In this test there were no shared-1 coordinate overlaps, so the correct output was a uniform 7x14 grid of 1s. Be careful to compare equal relative panel rows: bottom row index is separator+1+relative_row (here input row 8+r), not an unrelated row. A first incorrect candidate marked row3/col1 due misaligning a bottom marker; exact coordinate comparison shows none.

Additional confirmed recurrence (17x29): a uniform zero separator column at index 14 splits 17x14 panels (left columns 0–13, right columns 15–28). Left colors {9,2}, right colors {5,9}, shared S=9. Correct output is 17x14, 3 only where aligned left and right cells are both 9, otherwise 9. The 0-based coordinates producing 3 were (0,2), (1,10), (2,2), (2,9), (3,0), (5,5), (6,3), (8,1), (8,13), (9,10), and (13,0); submission confirmed correct with no wrong attempts.

Additional confirmed recurrence (12x15): uniform separator column 8 at index 7 splits two 12x7 panels, left columns 0–6 and right columns 8–14. Left colors {1,2}, right {1,4}, shared S=1. Compare same row and relative column. Output dimensions 12x7; output is 3 iff both aligned cells are 1, else 1. First submission incorrectly included (3,2) by overlooking the left marker; corrected output confirmed. Practical caution: explicitly scan for left-panel nonshared-color markers at candidate overlaps.')]
